patch_description:
The current hierarchical approach packs whole expert groups to fixed-size node buckets first, then replicates within each node with an equal number of physical slots per node. Since node token loads are unequal but slot counts are fixed, this creates systematic per-expert load imbalance (expert balancedness 0.25) and cross-node GPU imbalance.

The new approach drops the node hierarchy entirely and solves the problem globally in two stages:
1. Global water-filling replication: replicas are assigned to the hottest logical experts across the whole layer (vectorized over all layers simultaneously), which equalizes per-replica load `w_j/c_j` globally rather than per-node, directly improving expert balancedness.
2. Global LPT packing to GPUs with exact cardinality constraints (heap-based longest-processing-time-first), followed by a pairwise swap local-search refinement between the heaviest and lightest GPU that provably reduces the maximum GPU load until no improving swap exists. This improves GPU balancedness beyond plain greedy.

It also runs fully on vectorized NumPy with only short Python loops (num_redundant iterations for replication, one heap pass + bounded refinement per layer for packing), keeping algorithm runtime very low.
